rules.rule: Prefer ONE dominant quality per block when weekly hard-stress is already at cap; two qualities may progress together at moderate loads. This is a fatigue-budgeting heuristic, not an interference finding.
rules.programmingAction: Block Planner may set 1 dominant + 1-2 maintained qualities. The binding constraint is the hard-day budget (BUD-001), not the number of qualities. Never auto-enforced.

rules.rule: Do not apply beginner, obese, or elite-athlete evidence to this user without explicitly flagging it as extrapolated.
rules.programmingAction: Evidence Engine tags every decision with population + energyState; mismatches are surfaced, not hidden.

rules.rule: When sources conflict, resolve by evidence grade x population fit; ties break toward lower fatigue/injury cost; log the conflict and decision.
rules.programmingAction: Record conflicts in research/research-log.md (Contradicts prior beliefs section).

rules.rule: In a deficit, maintain load/intensity and cut volume first; do not chase net hypertrophy.
rules.programmingAction: Strength Engine holds top-set loads; Progression Engine reduces volume before load when fatigued.

rules.rule: Train each muscle group / movement pattern 2x per week.
rules.programmingAction: Strength Engine distributes each pattern across 2 sessions/wk.

rules.rule: Weekly volume 10-20 sets/muscle outside a deficit; cap at 10-14 sets/muscle during a deficit.
rules.programmingAction: Strength Engine targets 10-14 sets/muscle/wk in cut blocks; raise only if Readiness supports it.

rules.rule: Default proximity to failure 1-3 RIR; reserve 0-1 RIR for isolation/machine work; never to failure on compounds in a deficit.
rules.programmingAction: Strength Engine sets RIR targets per exercise; isolation may go 0-1 RIR.

rules.rule: Include at least one heavy slot (3-6 reps) per main movement pattern.
rules.programmingAction: Strength Engine guarantees a heavy primary per pattern per week.

rules.rule: Rest at least 2 min on compounds (2-3 min), 1-2 min on accessories.
rules.programmingAction: Strength Engine sets default rest by exercise role.

rules.rule: Use full ROM and emphasize lengthened (long muscle length) positions where joint-safe.
rules.programmingAction: Exercise Selection Engine prefers exercises loading the lengthened position.

rules.rule: Periodization model is hypertrophy-insensitive when volume/intensity are equated; for strength, undulating is modestly superior to linear in trained lifters, and any periodization beats none. Periodize for strength, variety and adherence, not for a hypertrophy advantage.
rules.programmingAction: Block Planner may use undulating loading for strength; expects no hypertrophy advantage from periodization style.

rules.rule: Keep main compounds stable for progression; rotate accessories at block boundaries (4-6 wk) with purpose, not weekly.
rules.programmingAction: Exercise Selection Engine rotates accessories only at block edges.

rules.rule: Protein 1.8-2.7 g/kg bodyweight; bias higher when leaner or in a larger deficit.
rules.programmingAction: Nutrition guidance enforces protein floor scaled to leanness/deficit.

rules.rule: Rate of loss is a dial of 0.5-1.0% bodyweight/week, governed by performance and wellness; go slower the leaner/more trained.
rules.programmingAction: Recovery/Progression Engines slow the deficit if strength or wellness trends decline.

rules.rule: Recomposition magnitude decreases with training age and leanness; set realistic expectations (slow simultaneous gain/loss in trained adults).
rules.programmingAction: Goal Engine frames trained-user recomp as slow; avoids promising both fast.

rules.rule: Exploit the return-from-layoff window: muscle-memory favors recomposition for the first weeks back.
rules.programmingAction: Block Planner prioritizes strength + adequate protein early to recapture lost mass.

rules.rule: Schedule maintenance diet breaks aligned with training deloads to improve fat-loss efficiency and blunt metabolic adaptation (NOT to preserve more lean mass).
rules.programmingAction: Block Planner co-locates diet breaks with deloads.

rules.rule: Drink 5-10 mL/kg bodyweight of fluid in the 2-4 h before a session (~500 mL for this user); keep within-session losses under 2% bodyweight.
rules.programmingAction: Nutrition guidance surfaces a pre-session hydration prompt; Cardio Engine raises it under ENV-001 heat conditions.

rules.rule: Periodise carbohydrate by day type rather than raising total intake: more on heavy-lower and long-cardio days, less on rest days, protein and weekly calories unchanged.
rules.programmingAction: Nutrition guidance maps the day's session family to a CHO target band.

rules.rule: Keep energy availability above ~30 kcal/kg FFM/day; treat sustained low EA as an upstream gate on training load, confirmed by symptoms rather than by the arithmetic alone.
rules.programmingAction: Recovery Engine treats 2+ worsening LEA markers over 2 weeks as a trigger for an early diet break plus a volume cut; never derives a calorie number from the EA estimate alone.

rules.rule: Hold a daily step floor (~7,000-10,000) through the deficit; NEAT falls spontaneously as energy intake drops.
rules.programmingAction: Surface the weekly step trend as adherence context; never convert steps into a calorie prescription.

rules.rule: Avoid hard running within 24h before heavy lower-body strength sessions.
rules.programmingAction: Interference Engine moves hard running away from lower-heavy days or swaps modality.

rules.rule: Running produces more lower-limb interference and impact than cycling/rowing/ski; prefer low-interference modality when legs are fatigued or impact must be limited.
rules.programmingAction: Modality Engine selects erg/bike over running when lower-limb load is high.

rules.rule: If strength and endurance share a session, lift first when strength is the priority.
rules.programmingAction: Strength/Cardio Engines order intra-session work by dominant goal.

rules.rule: Protect power/explosive work: place it fresh, early, never after endurance or under accumulated fatigue.
rules.programmingAction: Hybrid/Athleticism Engines place power microdosing at session start on fresh days.

rules.rule: Reject the claim that cardio inherently kills strength/hypertrophy; moderate cardio does not meaningfully blunt gains if volume is managed and not placed immediately pre-lift.
rules.programmingAction: Goal Engine treats cardio as co-equal, not a threat to be minimized.

rules.rule: Cap total endurance volume during strength-priority blocks.
rules.programmingAction: Block Planner caps weekly endurance when strength is dominant.

rules.rule: Keep roughly 80/20 easy/hard intensity distribution across the WHOLE week, not just running.
rules.programmingAction: Interacts with BUD-001/BUD-002 to bound weekly hard stress.

rules.rule: Anchor running zones to HR/RPE early; introduce pace targets later. Daniels VDOT paces are too fast for a 5k-novice.
rules.programmingAction: Cardio Engine prescribes zones by HR/RPE until aerobic base is established.

rules.rule: Progress running volume by ~10%/week soft cap with periodic down weeks.
rules.programmingAction: Progression Engine limits weekly running-volume jumps; Recovery Engine inserts down weeks.

rules.rule: Intervals max 1 session/week, never colliding with heavy legs.
rules.programmingAction: Cardio + Interference Engines limit and place interval days.

rules.rule: Measure Z2 aerobic improvement by aerobic decoupling (<5%) and pace-at-fixed-HR, not raw speed.
rules.programmingAction: Cardio + Readiness Engines track decoupling and pace-to-HR trends from Intervals.

rules.rule: Use run/walk intervals when aerobic base is low or HR drift is high.
rules.programmingAction: Cardio Engine prescribes run/walk in early running phase.

rules.rule: Maintain heavy strength and low-dose plyometrics during running blocks; they improve running economy.
rules.programmingAction: Block Planner keeps strength + plyo in maintenance even when running is dominant.

rules.rule: HIIT and MICT both raise VO2max; choose by fatigue cost, time, and specificity rather than dogma.
rules.programmingAction: Cardio Engine balances HIIT vs MICT against BUD-001.

rules.rule: Hybrid/HYROX-like frequency: 0-1 session/week in a cut or strength block; up to 2 only in a dedicated work-capacity block.
rules.programmingAction: Hybrid Engine bounds frequency by current block goal.

rules.rule: Hybrid conditioning counts as a hard day and a partial leg/systemic stressor; space it from heavy legs and hard runs.
rules.programmingAction: Interference Engine + BUD-002 place and weight hybrid sessions.

rules.rule: Under fatigue, use only low-skill movements in hybrid sessions (sled, carries, lunges, wall ball, ergs); no Olympic lifts or gymnastics.
rules.programmingAction: Exercise Selection Engine filters by skillRequirement under fatigue.

rules.rule: Hybrid benchmarks no more than once every 4-6 weeks; not a weekly session type.
rules.programmingAction: Block Planner schedules benchmarks at block edges only.

rules.rule: Use indoor low-impact hybrid (row/ski/bike/sled) when impact or lower-limb load must be limited.
rules.programmingAction: Modality + Hybrid Engines select low-impact stations when legs are loaded.

rules.rule: Plyometrics at low dose (~40-80 contacts/session), progress slowly, introduce after an aerobic/strength base.
rules.programmingAction: Athleticism Engine caps contacts and gates plyo behind base-building.

rules.rule: Microdose power work fresh at session start, low volume, maximal intent.
rules.programmingAction: Athleticism Engine places power before fatiguing work.

rules.rule: Prioritize anti-rotation / anti-extension core work (Pallof, dead bug, carries, ab wheel).
rules.programmingAction: Exercise Selection Engine favors anti-rotation/anti-extension core. Every strength week must contain >=1 core-anti-rotation AND >=1 core-anti-extension; flexion work is optional extra, never the whole allocation.

rules.rule: Introduce plyometrics only after aerobic and strength base; tendons adapt slowly.
rules.programmingAction: Block Planner sequences plyo after base blocks.

rules.rule: Unilateral lower-body training transfers comparably to bilateral for strength and adds knee/hip resilience and athletic carryover.
rules.programmingAction: Exercise Selection Engine includes unilateral lower (BSS, lunges, step-ups) for athleticism and joint resilience.

rules.rule: Hold a mobility/flexibility floor of 2-3 sessions per week, ~60 s total per major muscle-tendon unit.
rules.programmingAction: Block Planner keeps mobility slots on recovery/cardio days; Recovery Engine flags a week with fewer than 2.

rules.rule: Use 7-day rolling trends for HRV/RHR, not isolated daily values.
rules.programmingAction: Readiness Engine computes rolling means; ignores single-day spikes.

rules.rule: Require multi-signal confirmation (>=2 concordant signals) before changing the plan.
rules.programmingAction: Readiness Engine gates downgrades on concordant signals.

rules.rule: Treat Whoop Recovery score as a yellow/red flag, never as an exact dose calculator.
rules.programmingAction: Readiness Engine maps recovery to green/yellow/red only.

rules.rule: Interpret HRV against the individual's own baseline; never compare across people.
rules.programmingAction: Readiness Engine normalizes HRV to personal baseline.

rules.rule: When wearable scores conflict with actual performance and subjective state, prioritize performance + subjective feedback.
rules.programmingAction: Readiness Engine weights warm-up performance + subjective wellness above daily score.

rules.rule: Treat sleep (duration + consistency) as the primary recovery lever.
rules.programmingAction: Readiness Engine flags sleep debt; Recovery Engine prioritizes sleep interventions.

rules.rule: A red day changes the session OBJECTIVE (downgrade/replace), not merely the load.
rules.programmingAction: Readiness Engine (upstream gate) can swap a hard session for recovery work.

rules.rule: Trigger a deload on sustained multi-signal decline (HRV down + RHR up + performance down + wellness down).
rules.programmingAction: Recovery Engine triggers deload; reuses existing weekly-checkin LEA triggers.

rules.rule: Avoid abrupt load spikes and build chronic capacity as a PRINCIPLE; do not apply rigid ACWR thresholds.
rules.programmingAction: Progression + Recovery Engines smooth weekly load changes without rigid ratios.

rules.rule: For tendon issues, load progressively (isometrics/heavy-slow resistance); do not rest to zero.
rules.programmingAction: Recovery Engine substitutes progressive tendon loading, not removal.

rules.rule: On low-back pain, modify variant/ROM/load; do not reflexively remove strength training.
rules.programmingAction: Exercise Selection + Recovery Engines swap to lumbar-friendly variants.

rules.rule: Deload every 4-6 weeks, or reactively after two consecutive sessions of performance decline.
rules.programmingAction: Block Planner schedules deloads; Recovery Engine triggers reactive ones.

rules.rule: Machines and free weights produce similar hypertrophy/strength when matched; choose by ROI, stability, joint comfort, and fatigue.
rules.programmingAction: Exercise Selection Engine prefers machines when systemically taxed or for high-fatigue isolation.

rules.rule: Select exercises by stimulus-to-fatigue ratio and joint-stress profile, not novelty or variety for its own sake.
rules.programmingAction: Exercise Selection Engine ranks candidates by qualitative SFR buckets.

rules.rule: Do not use EMG amplitude as a direct proxy for hypertrophy; ignore EMG-based exercise hype.
rules.programmingAction: Evidence Engine flags EMG-only justifications as weak.

rules.rule: Select cardio modality by impact + interference + recent lower-limb load + goal specificity.
rules.programmingAction: Modality Engine uses cardio metadata to pick run/treadmill/bike/row/ski.

rules.rule: No more than 2-3 truly hard sessions per week counting ALL modalities (heavy strength, intervals, threshold, hard hybrid, demanding long run).
rules.programmingAction: See hard-day-budget.md; Block Planner + Interference Engine enforce the cap.

rules.rule: Assign each session a hard-stress weight and keep the weekly sum under the block's budget cap.
rules.programmingAction: See hard-day-budget.md for weights and cap; engines sum and constrain.

rules.rule: Treat cardiorespiratory fitness as a health outcome in its own right, not only as a means to body composition: the fitness-mortality gradient is steep and shows no upper limit of benefit.
rules.programmingAction: Goal Engine keeps a minimum aerobic dose even in strength-dominant blocks; the aerobic quality is never the first thing cut for convenience.

rules.rule: Keep resistance training in the plan for health reasons independent of hypertrophy or aesthetics; ~30-60 min/week of muscle-strengthening activity carries most of the mortality benefit.
rules.programmingAction: Block Planner never drops strength below 2 sessions/wk; the minimum-dose variant is framed as health-preserving, not as a failure week.

rules.rule: Track health markers longitudinally and surface them as context; never derive treatment from them. Abnormal markers are a referral, not a programming input.
rules.programmingAction: Surface marker trends and staleness in the profile; flag when a panel is older than ~12 months; never gate a session on a lab value.

rules.rule: Protect habitual sleep duration in the 7-8 h range as a longevity target, not only a recovery lever; both short and long sleep associate with higher mortality.
rules.programmingAction: Readiness Engine surfaces the rolling sleep trend against a 7-8 h band; Recovery Engine prioritises sleep before any other intervention.

rules.rule: In the heat, hold the HR target and let pace fall; do not chase the usual pace. For the same power output, heart rate rises with heat strain, so an HR-anchored easy run is simply slower in August.
rules.programmingAction: Cardio Engine keeps zone/HR as the target in heat and annotates pace expectations; Readiness Engine suppresses pace-based aerobic-progress claims during hot months.

rules.rule: Move hard or long sessions indoors, or to the cooler ends of the day, when heat is high; raise fluid intake above the REC-006 baseline and treat heat as a hard-day cost multiplier.
rules.programmingAction: Modality Engine prefers indoor low-impact options in heat (reuses INT-002/HYB-005 machinery); Nutrition guidance raises the REC-006 pre-session dose.
